newsitem.title: USA: Boston Scientific, Target to merge.
newsitem.headline: Boston Scientific, Target to merge.

text.p: Boston Scientific Corp. said it agreed to acquire Target Therapeutics Inc. in a stock swap valued at $1.1 billion, the medical device manufacturers said in a joint statement.
Under terms of the tax-free transaction, Boston Scientific will swap 1.07 shares of its common shares for each Target common share.
The deal, which is subject to approval by regulators and Target shareholders, is expected to close during the second quarter of 1997, the companies said.
Target Therapeutics, headquartered in Fremont, Calif., makes catheter-based disposable and implantable medical devices used to treat neurovascular diseases.
The company's products are used to treat diseased, ruptured or blocked blood vessels in the brain that cause strokes.

One of these products, the Guglielmi detachable coil system, is used to treat the rupture of cerebral aneurysms. It is the only device approved by the FDA for treatment of inoperable or high-risk intracranial aneurysms.
Boston Scientific also makes medical devices.
Analysts said the acquisition gives Boston Scientific, a strong footing in the interventional neural radiology, or INR market.

"Bottom line, it's a great move for Boston Scientific," said Sanjiv Arora, an analyst at Dain Bosworth. "It's a lot of money to pay, but it gets them (Boston Scientific) an A-player in the INR market."
